Candidate research mechanism: knowledge requires a proposition/environment-dependent, non-uniform margin for error separating known-true cases from false cases via a buffer of true-but-unknown cases; explicitly NOT a scalar confidence/probability (Margin != Confidence, Epistemic-quality != scalar score), reinforcing KnowledgeOS's existing anti-score stance; suggests a margin/buffer structure between False, True-Unknown and Known rather than another flat categorical value.

Candidate three-way refinement of UNKNOWN, adapted from Williamson's structural-unknowability chapter: Unknown_current (potentially resolvable with more evidence), Unknown_access (resolvable in principle but not from current access/capability), Unknown_structural (not resolvable by the relevant epistemic system even in principle) -- extends the prior UnknownDimension != UnknownValue distinction and directly strengthens Zero != IncompleteWork / Unknown != ResolvableGap.

notations: True(p) not=> Knowable(p) not=> Accessible(p,Gamma) not=> Known(p,Gamma)

Candidate rule that asserting p creates a candidate responsibility for p's truth, mapped onto the existing Claim->Evidence->Determination->Decision chain and the claimant/evidence/justification/authority/standing separation; explicitly not adopted as a KnowledgeOS primitive, and used to argue LLM-confidence != Knowledge and GeneratedAssertion != Determination (anti-reasoner/deterministic-kernel boundary).

notations: Evaluation = Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance x Accessibility

Candidate formal framework (deontic logic: permission/obligation/prohibition, is/ought distinction) proposed for the open KnowledgeOS Authority/Governance TODO.

Williamson's core thesis that knowledge cannot be analysed into belief+truth+justification (no non-circular X exists, per the Gettier literature and a 'red != coloured+X' analogy); translated as KnowledgeOS should treat Knowledge as a primitive status assignable to epistemic states, not a derived/analysed property. Adopted (checked) in this extraction's summary table.

Formal Fitch's-paradox argument (knowledge distributes over conjunction + factivity => no one can know an unknown truth => weak verificationism (all truths knowable) entails all truths are known, hence not all truths are knowable given not all are known) plus a Moorean-twist variant (it is impossible to know that p is true-and-unknown); translated as: KnowledgeOS cannot represent 'known unknown' knowledge -- a gap/Zero/boundary cannot be known AS a gap/Zero/boundary.

notations: P1: all evidence propositional; P2: all propositional evidence is knowledge; P3: all knowledge is evidence

Candidate representation of the KnowledgeOS evaluator/reasoner itself as a formal system S=(language L, axioms A, inference rules R, derivability relation Der, semantic interpretation Sem), distinguishing derivability (Gamma |-_S p) from model-truth (M |= p).

Candidate mechanically-checkable Proof object (formal system, conclusion, derivation sequence pi) and a distinct DerivationEvidence category (with provenance lambda) that supports S|-p without automatically establishing Truth(p) unless soundness is separately established; includes a concrete ProofArtifact schema (systemId/systemVersion/premises/inferenceRules/derivationSteps/conclusion/encoding/hash/provenance) and VerifyProof(pi,S,p)->{True,False}, argued to be closer to a deterministic kernel operation than an LLM-generated explanation.

KnowledgeOS must never silently implement 'proved -> true' without recording which soundness theorem/assumption licenses the transition; converse also fails for sufficiently expressive systems (incompleteness: Truth does not imply Derivability); VerifyProof yields Derivable_S(p) only, and Sound(S) & Derivable_S(p) -> Truth(p) requires an explicit separately-established bridge.

Candidate independent dimension DerivabilityStatus, distinguishing Unknown_S (current formal system cannot decide p) from Unknown_evidence/Unknown_access/Unknown_structural; labels must not be confused with truth or epistemic standing. [PROP].

Candidate ordering S1 prec S2 (S2 has stronger reasoning resources) such that a statement undecidable in S1 may be decidable in S2 while S2 acquires new undecidable statements of its own; gives a formal foundation for 'higher reasoning context', and parallels Williamson's current-vs-structural-unknowability distinction, jointly supporting 'Unknown is indexed by epistemic/formal context'.

Candidate core anti-collapse principle: object-level p, meta-level Provable_S(p), and meta-meta-level Provable_S(Provable_S(p)) must not be automatically interchangeable absent an explicit bridge; explicitly aligned with Williamson's K(p) not=> K(K(p)) as a second independent reason for level separation, extended to Verified(p) != Verified(Verified(p)).

notations: B = B_data ∪ B_access ∪ B_representation ∪ B_reasoning ∪ B_formal
note: Candidate decomposition of Zero's boundary examination into five distinct sources: missing evidence/data, inaccessible evidence, inadequate representation, evaluator/reasoner limitation, and formal undecidability/incompleteness (FormalBoundary_S(p), explicitly != Absence, != False, != NoEvidence); a strong candidate, not adopted.

Applies Godel's second incompleteness theorem (a sufficiently expressive system cannot prove its own consistency with only its own resources) to reject 'Kernel verifies Kernel'; proposes an Assurance Ladder S0 prec S1 prec S2... where each level can establish properties of the previous level unavailable internally, researched as KR-META-ASSURANCE (not adopted); extends the Verification chain with Verification->AssuranceContext, requiring Verification(p,S) to record AssuranceBasis(S).

Candidate rule that Completeness is always relative to a formal system and semantics; KnowledgeOS must never write 'KnowledgeOS = Complete' and must ban unqualified Complete(x) in favor of dimension-qualified variants (Complete_S/Complete_E/Complete_K/Complete_G), fitting the existing NoKnownGap != Complete principle.

Candidate principle that Determination is system-relative -- Determination(p|S,Gamma) depends on available formal language, axioms, inference rules, evidence, context, computational resources and accessibility -- while Truth(p) may remain fixed even as Determination(p|S1) and Determination(p|S2) differ.

aliases: Derivability, Truth and Formal Boundary experiment
note: Proposed experiment testing a small formal system S against ten proposition types (derivable-and-true, derivable-without-truth-bridge, refutable, undecidable-in-S, decidable-in-stronger-S', evidence-supported-but-not-derivable, derivable-after-extension, meta-level statement, consistency statement, statement-about-a-proof) to test whether the current representation distinguishes Truth/Derivable/Refutable/Undecidable/MetaLevel/Accessible/Known without collapsing them; argued more important than another flat-value experiment since the missing structure is relational, not merely a larger enum.

notations: e,w |= O alpha iff forall w': w' in e iff e,w'|=alpha
note: Formal O operator: e |= O alpha iff e consists exactly of the worlds where alpha is true, i.e. 'alpha is ALL that is known'; characterizes ASK/TELL via |=(OKB=>Kalpha) and |=(OKB=>K(alpha==phi)); a 'determinate' sentence uniquely determines an epistemic state and every determinate sentence is equivalent (under O) to some objective sentence -- proposed as the formal basis for KnowledgeOS Zero ('having a KB means these sentences are all that is known... implies not believing others').

notations: e|_pi = {w | w|=c for all c in Gamma_{e,pi}}
note: Formal O(pi) operator: 'all the agent knows about subject matter pi is alpha', constructed via e-pi-minimal clauses and prime implicates of phi mentioning pi; proposed as the formal basis for Boundary (what is known vs not known about a specific topic) and for focused/relevance queries.

aliases: tractable explicit belief avoiding logical omniscience
note: Tractable alternative to K using four-valued situations (true-only/false-only/both/neither) where beliefs are NOT closed under implication or logical consequence (avoiding logical omniscience), with complexity results (co-NP-complete propositional tautological entailment; polynomial CNF; undecidable/decidable first-order variants depending on existential generalization); directly parallels the project's own FDE (four-valued) evaluation work.

notations: K exists x P(x) != exists x K P(x)
note: Formal de dicto (K-exists-x-P(x), it is known a P exists) vs de re (exists-x-K-P(x), a specific x is known to be P) distinction, with de re implying de dicto but not conversely; translated as: KnowledgeOS evaluation must distinguish knowing THAT a requirement is satisfied from knowing WHICH requirement/instance satisfies it.

Formal theorem that finitely-representable epistemic states are closed under TELL (representable states are NOT closed under TELL in general), proved via a RES/reduction function eliminating K-operators into objective formulas capturing known instances; proposed as a compiler-like mechanism reducing epistemic queries to objective entailment.

Formal stable-set (closed under FOL consequence, K-introspective, negative-introspective) and stable-expansion definitions connecting Only-Knowing to autoepistemic logic (e|=O-alpha iff e's basic belief set is a stable expansion of {alpha}), with a propositional computation algorithm; proposed as the formal basis for computing 'only-known' content, nonmonotonic defaults, and CWA-as-only-knowing.

Candidate relation formalizing that a determination must actually be BASED ON (grounded/explained by) evidence, not merely co-occur with good evidence (the stopped-clock/Gettier phenomenon); distinguishes Evidence-exists != Evidence-supports != Determination-based-on-evidence != Determination-produced-by-reliable-process. Status: [STRONG DERIVATION CANDIDATE], not yet a Theory v1.3 primitive.

Candidate that knowledge depends on the process producing a belief/determination, not merely on evidence possessed; process P=(type,implementation,inputs,outputs,environment,provenance) with an evaluable Reliable(P,Gamma) property that is explicitly environment-relative (a process reliable in one environment may be unreliable in another); motivates Evaluation(P,E,Gamma) rather than Evaluation(P,E), relevant to but not resolving the open phi (frame) decision. Also separates EvidenceQuality(e,Gamma) from ProcessReliability(P,Gamma) from Basing(e,P,d,Gamma), giving DeterminationAdequacy = Evidence+Basing+Process+Context as distinct inspectable dimensions (not a value equation).

Distinguishes ordinary provenance (where an artifact came from) from epistemic provenance (why a determination exists: source, acquisition, originating evidence, transforming process, accepting evaluator, context); grounded in the memory/source-monitoring 'forgotten evidence' problem (a determination can persist after its original supporting evidence becomes inaccessible); current inaccessibility of evidence must not be equated with it never having supported the determination. Status: [STRONG DERIVATION], belongs close to core theory.

Candidate distinction between what a system actually does to produce a determination (descriptive) and what conditions make that process epistemically acceptable (normative/governance question); principle: never infer epistemic validity merely from a process having successfully produced an output (guards e.g. against retrieval->LLM-synthesis->unsupported-assumption->answer being treated as automatically valid).

notations: InformationEffect(delta) in {preservative, extractive/deductive, expansive/inductive, reconstructive, evaluative}

Candidate distinction (from the skepticism discussion) that possessing knowledge/standing is separate from having sufficient evidence/confidence to assert or defend it, judged 'extraordinarily compatible' with a prior R1 decision (factivity retained externally, verification separate from factivity); supports keeping Standing/Assurance/Verification/Decision/Authorization as separate concepts, and separately argues pragmatic encroachment (KnowledgeStanding derived from Risk/Stake) and contextualism (K(p,Gamma1)!=K(p,Gamma2) purely from context) should both be REJECTED, preserving KnowledgeStanding != DecisionThreshold while allowing DecisionThreshold=f(Knowledge,Risk,Authority,Purpose).

Candidate that Reliability(P,Gamma) may be a property of a network/distributed process (social externalism, extended-mind: epistemic process boundaries need not coincide with agent boundaries -- e.g. human+retrieval+database+calculator+AI+verifier as one production chain, components preserved rather than collapsed into one 'knower'); explicitly a research candidate, not adopting 'SocialExternalism' or 'ExtendedMind' as KnowledgeOS primitives. Also: Presentation != Reliability, AuthorityCue != EvidenceQuality, Confidence != Truth, SourceReliability != EvidenceTruth != DeterminationStanding (source-monitoring/testimony arguments).

Deductive validity preserves truth without adding information beyond the premises; induction extends beyond the premises without deductive certainty; explicitly not proposed as 'Deduction vs Induction' KnowledgeOS primitives but as instances of the more general InformationEffect(delta) property.

aliases: Basing, Process Reliability and Epistemic Lineage
note: Proposed research artifact with five experiments: S1 Basing (test Basing(E,D) against unused/used/misleading/competing/accidentally-matching evidence), S2 Process Reliability (six processes P1-P6 producing the same conclusion via calculation/intuition/unreliable-sensor/stale-cache/testimony/AI-inference), S3 Epistemic Lineage (forgotten/superseded/corrected evidence scenarios), S4 Assurance vs Standing (knows-but-cannot-defend vs weak-evidence-belief vs strong-evidence-false-conclusion vs verified), S5 Distributed Process (individual vs multi-node human+AI+retrieval+verification chain).

(query) is distinct from 'should p receive Standing=positive?' (evaluation) and 'should p become a determination?' (determination).

notations: Derivable_S(p) vs Accessible_S(p) vs ExplicitlyRepresented(p) vs Determined(p)

aliases: Explicit/Implicit Knowledge, Query, Boundary and Transition experiment
note: Proposed experiment with 14 test cases (E1-E14): explicit-no-derivation, explicit-with-derivable-consequence, logically-derivable-but-not-computed, true-but-unrepresented-and-underivable, existential-without-identified-instance, identified-instance (de re), contradictory explicit beliefs, unknown-from-no-information, unknown-from-reasoning-limits, unknown-from-out-of-boundary subject matter, TELL-then-reasoning, action changing one fluent while another persists, action changing representation but not truth, and identical representation under two reasoning systems; connects to Contr/Zero/Gap/semantic-identity/delta/Projection without prematurely deciding any of them.

notations: D = Sigma ∪ D_ss ∪ D_ap ∪ D_una ∪ D_S0
note: Full formal decomposition of a situation-calculus domain theory into foundational axioms Sigma, successor-state axioms D_ss, action-precondition axioms D_ap, unique-names axioms D_una, and an initial database D_S0 (sentences uniform in S0, i.e. not mentioning Poss/sqsubset or the future); Relative Satisfiability Theorem: D is satisfiable iff D_una ∪ D_S0 is.

Condition-action interrupt rules compiled into Golog test-then-action macros, combined via a DoR semantics that interleaves execution of program A with a set of Rules, allowing exogenous actions/interrupts after each primitive action.

Stochastic action decomposition (agent-controlled action, nature choosing among outcome actions via a choice predicate and probability function), stDo recursive probability-of-execution definition, and an MDP value/expected-value formalism (value/reward/cost per step, eValue integrating over initial-state probabilities and execution probabilities); policies as stGolog programs with sensing-conditioned branches.

Formal progression definition (a set of S_alpha-uniform sentences such that every model of the progressed theory has a same-future-behavior model of the original theory), with progression not always first-order definable (finite progression is second-order definable); STRIPS operators (precondition/delete-list/add-list) formalized as a special case of progression with a correctness theorem equating STRIPS plans to situation-calculus plans for suitable basic action theories.

aliases: FORMAL REPRESENTATION, REASONING AND EPISTEMIC CHANGE
note: A 17-section theory-backlog candidate distinct from (but overlapping and extending) the Levesque-Lakemeyer-derived FR.1-FR.10: adds a reasoning-system tuple S=(L,Sigma,R,Sem,B) (FR.3), Evaluation/Determination as explicit stages (FR.5-FR.6), Revision/Contraction/Update as three DISTINCT epistemic-change operations (FR.7-FR.9), Temporal State and Persistence-as-transition-property (FR.10-FR.11), Representation Adequacy (FR.12), Computational Boundedness (FR.13), Task Knowledge != Domain Knowledge != Reasoning Mechanism (FR.14), Problem-Solving Method (FR.15), Epistemic Lineage (FR.16), and Multiple Compatible Models allowing underdetermined-but-not-false determination (FR.17).

Distinguishes three causes of state change: Revision (new information about an otherwise static world), Contraction (removing a commitment, possibly requiring removal of dependent derived commitments), and Update (responding to actual world change rather than correcting incomplete belief) -- explicitly 'Revision and world change must never be conflated' (section 10, not read in full but referenced from the promote-table); extended with NewComputationalCapability->NewDerivation and NewObservation->Evidence as further distinct causes of change.

Formal proposal defining R_req as a set of semantic distinctions (each an equivalence relation on the state space S) that any KnowledgeOS knowledge-representation language or projection must preserve; directly targets the R_req TODO left open throughout this batch.

notations: K preserves d iff forall s1,s2: s1 not-sim_d s2 => E(s1)!=E(s2)
pi is R_req-adequate iff forall d in R_req: preserved through pi∘E
note: Formal criteria: an encoding K collapses a distinction d if two d-inequivalent states map to the same encoding; a transformation/projection pi is R_req-adequate if it preserves every distinction in R_req through composition with the encoding E.

notations: AbsenceOfEvidence iff phi not-in K and not-phi not-in K
EvidenceOfAbsence iff exists e in E: e |- not-phi
note: Formal iff-definitions for AbsenceOfEvidence (neither phi nor not-phi is in the knowledge base) versus EvidenceOfAbsence (some evidence entails not-phi), cited as grounded in a prior 'Zero Lens Specification' (Non-collapse Invariant #3) and marked Tier P1 Core Invariant; the structural comparison matrix shows this distinction is collapsed by classical, 3-valued, AND 4-valued FDE logics alike, and preserved only by the proposed R_req.

Two-part verification suite for any proposed kernel/projection pi: the Separation Test (for every pair of distinct values in any distinction d, two minimal test states must map to different encodings, else verification FAILS with distinction collapsed) and the Round-Trip Transformation Test (for a projection f and reconstruction g, applying g after f must preserve every distinction in R_req).

Three-tier prioritization: P1 (Epistemic Status, Justification Mode, Temporal Currency, Absence-vs-Evidence-of-Absence) must be preserved by all core kernels/projections; P2 (Allen relations, Resolution Status, Scope Boundary, Intensional Identity) must be natively supported by the top-level KR language; P3 (deontic/normative distinctions, fine-grained probability) is extended/domain-specific.

Ten distinctions proposed for addition to R_req, sourced from classical philosophy of language/logic/modality rather than KnowledgeOS-native experiments: Analytic/Synthetic (Quine 1951), A Priori/A Posteriori (Kant, Kripke), Necessary/Contingent (Kripke 1980), Truth/Validity (Tarski 1936, Tier 1), Soundness/Completeness (Godel 1931), Decidability/Undecidability (Church/Turing), Local/Global (KR literature), Intentional/Extensional (Fagin et al. 1995), De Dicto/De Re (Hintikka 1962), Intrinsic/Extrinsic (action theory).

notations: 5 criteria: Distinction Preservation, Transformation Invariance, Projection Adequacy, Composition Preservation, Zero Compliance
aliases: critique of R_req's verification test suite
note: Reviews five verification criteria (more than the two-part suite seen in S2551), each with a strength, a weakness, and a fix: Distinction Preservation needs a context parameter; Transformation Invariance needs an exception for intentional distinction-modifying transformations; Projection Adequacy is 'too strong' and should allow Tier 2/3 loss but not Tier 1; Composition Preservation should be verified only for core compositions (full verification may be impossible); Zero Compliance should additionally require all Tier 1 distinctions to be represented.
